补充讨论：前两条分别从产品设计和使用者角度展开，形成“结构复杂度”与“维修价值”的讨论；第三条主要是对链接可用性的简短回应，与洗衣机技术主题关联较弱。

49780226.article_content:
A few months ago our whirlpool washer wouldn’t spin.  It did everything else, but it was pretty worthless without the spin function because the clothes would just be sitting at the bottom of it completely soaked after a wash.   Of course, the first thing I did was go to Google and type in “Whirlpool washer won’t spin” and got a lot of hits on some great websites.  Most of them were repair websites and forums sponsored by kind individuals who freely share their knowledge such as
fixitnow.com
.   Others are sponsored by companies who sell parts to DIY homeowners, like
repairclinic.com
.
The forums always suggest the most common and easy fixes first, like the lid switch, which wasn’t my problem.  So I had to start disassembling the washer because the next item on the list was the coupling on the motor.  Fortunately, these websites have directions on how to get the washer open, which takes very little effort, as long as you know which screws to remove and in what order. I knew that the coupling was unlikely to be the failed item because the agitator was still working and it would be unlikely that a failed coupling would allow that to work.  Then I started looking at the clutch/brake mechanism and that also looked OK.    Finally, I figured it had to be the transmission, one of the hardest items to remove.  I had the entire washer torn apart and moved to the kitchen because our laundry room is more of an alcove in the entryway between the garage and the kitchen.
After pulling the transmission, I was faced with the prospect of taking it apart, knowing it would be filled with heavy oil.
To pull your washer’s transmission, you need to remove a bolt at the top of the shaft holding it to the agitator.  To expose that bolt, you have to pull off the plastic cap on the top of agitator as well as another translucent seal below it.  Note the translucent cap has an o-ring seal on it.  Make sure to put it back in properly when you re-assemble the washer to keep water out of that bolt’s compartment or it will rust and fuse with the shaft.
I carefully took out all the screws holding on the transmission’s top cover and drained the oil into a jar.   This was going to a really messy job and so I put on some vinyl mechanics gloves.
I was amazed at the complexity of the transmission.  It has to perform several functions, all without any input other than the direction the motor.  For instance, it has to agitate, spin, and also go into neutral without any shifters or solenoids.  The same motor is simultaneously running the pump from a portion of the drive shaft that comes out the other end.  The transmission uses a rather complex plate of pawls, gears, and cams on something called the ‘rack retainer’.   I was trying to simulate spinning the motor forward and backward and thus I could shift it from spin mode to agitate mode, but I couldn’t get it into spin.  It was then that I realized that something called a ‘shoulder pawl stud’ was broken off at its threads and the rack retainer was spinning freely.  This pawl stud works as an axle and also as a way of getting the plate to spin along with the spin gear, but it was broken with its threads embedded in the main gear.  So I had to find a new pawl stud and figure out a way to extract the threads from the hole they were in.  I was pretty sure that the threads had some locking compound on them and they weren’t going to come out easily.
The pawl stud wasn’t available as a separate part, but there was something called the
Neutral Drain Pack from Repairclinic.com
which included a lot of parts, including 2 different studs, since Whirlpool evidently beefed up the threads for the newer models, no doubt because it was a weak point.  The upside to that is that if I ruined the threads extracting the broken stud, I could drill and tap it for the larger stud and newer rack retainer.  So as my wife headed off to the laundry mat with a load of wash, I order the parts on line.  The neutral drain kit was about $17 + $6 shipping.    In the meantime, I tried to drill the screw threads out of the main drive gear.  I broke a drill bit doing it, but got enough of a hole down through the middle of the broken screw shaft that I thought I’d have success with an ‘easy out’.   I took it into work and borrowed an easy out and with the help of an arbor press to apply pressure to the easy out, I extracted the broken screw without doing any damage to the threads.
A few days later, the parts arrived.  The kit contained a lot more parts than I needed.  I replaced all the old parts with new ones, figuring after 15 years of service, there was no point in reassembling things with old parts when I had new ones right there.  Getting everything back together required some head scratching, but after thinking it through, I was able to manually operate the transmission and check the agitate and neutral modes.

data.author: xabd
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Noodle Gallery 与 Immich 的关系及其改进功能，重点争议在于应称其为“替代品”还是 Immich 的分支。

不同观点：
• chrismorgan 认为标题将其描述为“Google Photos 和 Immich 的替代品”并不准确；Noodle Gallery 实际上是 Immich 的软分支，通过加入特定功能形成差异，并提供了与 Immich 的对比说明。  
• bastawhiz 进一步强调，它不是严格意义上的 Immich 替代品，而是会随 Immich 每次发布持续 rebase（同步上游更新）的 fork。  
• y-c-o-m-b 关注实际使用痛点：Immich 的“伙伴共享”和人脸识别需要按账户重复承担处理开销，属于重大设计疏漏；他认为 Noodle Gallery 明确解决了这些问题，并因此表示认可和愿意采用。

补充讨论：争议主要是产品定位和措辞，而非功能价值。评论者基本认可 Noodle Gallery 针对多账户共享、人脸识别开销等问题的改进，但对其是否应被称为独立替代品存在分歧。

补充讨论：争议主要是产品定位和措辞，而非功能价值。评论者基本认可 Noodle Gallery 针对多账户共享、人脸识别开销等问题的改进，但对其是否应被称为独立替代品存在分歧。

data.author: semidror
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：macOS 27 中 Siri/Apple Intelligence 的整合引发了存储占用、隐私、可禁用性及实际用途的讨论。

不同观点：
• 存储与资源负担：有人认为本地 AI 占用基础款 Mac 约10%空间，Mac mini 用户称其“杀死”了可用容量；也有人担心后台服务持续消耗 CPU。  
• 隐私与控制权：评论者希望彻底关闭 Apple Intelligence，并建议使用企业配置文件、Screen Time 中切换“Siri Classic”，或停用相关 launchd 任务；但后者可能需要关闭 SIP，风险较高。  
• 系统机制变化：有人指出原 Spotlight 界面进程已改名为 Siri，怀疑 Spotlight 已被新的 Siri AI 完全替代，因此即使关闭 Siri，相关组件可能仍在运行。  
• Siri 的实际价值：部分用户几乎从未在 Mac 上主动使用 Siri，认为它功能有限；但也有人在手机上用它设置计时器、导航和拨打联系人，说明使用场景存在设备差异。  
• 语言与地区限制：Mac 系统语言和 Siri 语言必须一致才能使用 Apple Intelligence；有评论称该限制曾被取消，后又在 macOS 27 重新引入。  
• 对 macOS 27 的整体评价：有人希望欧盟版本功能较少、升级影响较小并暂缓升级；另有人批评新版本及测试版 bug 多，且旧问题反复出现。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于 Apple 是否提供了真正彻底、易用且不牺牲系统功能的关闭选项，以及 AI 的存储和后台成本是否值得其有限的实用性。

data.title: ZuckOff is a free app that sees Meta glasses before they see you
data.author: choult
data.article_summary: 波兰开发者Pawel Szydlowski推出免费应用ZuckOff，通过扫描蓝牙信号识别附近的Ray-Ban Meta、Oakley Meta和Snap Spectacles，并以信号强度估算距离。应用无法判断眼镜是否正在录像或识别佩戴者，但为防范隐蔽拍摄提供了辅助。文章同时指出，智能眼镜销量增长、指示灯易被遮挡，引发严重隐私与公共安全担忧，Meta已计划加强防篡改检测。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一款用于侦测附近智能眼镜/蓝牙设备的应用，讨论其与开源替代品的比较、可靠性、隐私伦理及产品定位。

不同观点：
• 质疑应用本身：有人认为它是“vibecoded”的可疑专有软件，已有运行较久的开源 Nearby Glasses 可替代；弹出购买周边、设置 Pro 付费功能，也加剧了不信任。
• 支持其实际价值：有人认为 AI 化并非问题，这是针对“不该存在却已普遍存在的偷拍风险”的快速解决方案。
• 质疑检测效果：应用似乎只在眼镜处于配对模式时有效；“未检测到”不代表没人录制，“检测到”也不代表确实在录制，因此信号难以指导日常行为。
• 关注隐私与监管：建议建立“请勿拍摄”标准，通过蓝牙发送可轮换的人脸标识，让相机自动打码；也有人建议法律要求录制眼镜在正面展示明显标志，并质问未经同意被持续拍摄为何被接受。
• 反思营销：有人讽刺宣传文案堆砌“证据”“记录所有蓝牙设备”等无关技术细节，并调侃其反监控定位和品牌命名。

补充讨论：评论还提到科幻小说《量子盗贼》中可精细控制他人对自己的感知，作为隐私保护的联想。主要争议集中在：产品是否可信、检测是否真正有效，以及偷拍防护应依靠个人工具还是法律和行业标准。

49785397.article_content:
ZuckOff
, a free Bluetooth detection app built by 30-year-old Polish developer Pawel Szydlowski, will tell you whether there is a pair of smart glasses in the room with you. In its launch month, it was reportedly
downloaded
by over 5,000 people on Apple’s App Store. As of writing, it had been downloaded 1,000 times on the Google Play Store.
Meta Is Charging a Subscription for Smart Glasses Features. Welcome to the New Era of Consumer Tech
You bought the hardware. Now you’ll need to subscribe for “expanded access” to the most advanced features.
By
Julian Chokkattu
Meta’s smart glasses have had a
hefty share of scrutiny
over the past few months. Unsolicited filming is a growing public safety concern, with venues like schools and cinemas increasingly banning their usage outright.
Szydlowski recorded the Bluetooth signals broadcast by various models of smart glasses, building a digital fingerprint for each of them. He bought the hardware himself to compile the data that flags when a unique identifier matches up with a manufacturer identifier, catching models like Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta and Snap Spectacles in the vicinity.
A
BBC investigation
in January traced dozens of accounts that posted content filmed with Meta glasses, one of which posted a 21-year-old woman’s face and phone number, amassing over 1.3 million views.
The recording indicator light on these glasses have proven fairly easy to defeat with a bit of tape, allowing a growing number of wearers to record without being detected. Roughly
seven million pairs
of Meta’s smart glasses were sold in 2025.
In July, Meta
announced
that it would push an update to detect when an LED light has been “physically tampered with or destroyed” and stop people from being able to film using those cameras. In an Instagram video, Meta chief technology officer Andrew Bosworth stated that they designed this camera to be noticed by the people around you. This is despite the fact that one of the product's key commercial propositions is that the camera doesn't look like a camera.
ZuckOff is not, however, able to tell you whether a pair of glasses nearby is recording, nor can it tell you who is wearing them. It reads signal strength to give you rough proximity information, which turns an invisible problem into a partially visible one, which at the very least is worth something until legislators take further global action.
It's also a pretty difficult thing for Meta to legally take down, since it isn’t intercepting anything and the signals the app reads are legal. The hardware is as easy as it is cheap to copy and paste. Its basic scanning feature is free on iPhone, and a ZuckOff Pro version is available to purchase, with additional features like continuous background monitoring, widgets, alerts, sighting history and CSV export.
Napster Is Back and It Wants to Digitally Clone Your Teacher
Once the music industry’s biggest headache, Napster’s next act is bringing AI to the classroom.
Iain Akerman
ZuckOff Is a Free App That Sees Meta Glasses Before They See You
You can't always tell if someone is recording you with their smart glasses – but your phone can help.
Megan Tomos

Viral videos of humanoid robots falling look like slapstick. But they expose the limits of technology being readied for work and war.
Malak Saleh

data.title: Ars Technica's Mac Mini review: The new M6 impresses but the price hike is rough
data.author: throw0101c
data.article_summary: 文章评测了2026款M6 Mac mini。其延续M4时代的小巧设计和接口布局，新增M6芯片，采用12核CPU、12核GPU，较M5多核性能更强，并支持最多三台显示器及更高内存带宽。但基础款涨至899美元，相比2024年M4版贵300美元，性价比明显下降。主要缺点仍是电源键位置不便，且仅配雷雳4接口。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕苹果 M6 相比 M1 的性能提升、产品耐用性、价格策略及购买价值展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 性能与耐用性：magicmicah85认为，M6终于在单核性能上约六年后达到 M1 的两倍；M1 Mac mini 和 MacBook Pro 长期稳定使用，反而说明苹果设备耐用，用户缺乏升级的必要性，影响了后续购买。
• 价格与生态吸引力：datakan认为苹果产品涨价促使其回到 Windows；既然价格高昂，Windows还能兼顾与孩子玩游戏，而目前苹果除 iPhone 外缺乏明显优势。
• 参数准确性：adgjlsfhk1质疑 L1 缓存数据，认为“E 核心缓存大于 P 核心”不太合理，但也提出低频率可能让这种设计成为可能，焦点在规格表是否有误及架构原因。
• 性价比与特定用途：AnotherGoodName计划等待约200美元的翻新 M4，认为其适合作为低功耗的 tmux 终端，体现出对低价、实用型设备的认可。

补充讨论：评论之间的核心分歧在于苹果设备的长期耐用性是否抵消高价格：有人因设备太耐用而不愿升级，也有人认为涨价削弱了苹果相对 Windows 的吸引力。

The
new Mac mini
is the kind of Mac upgrade Apple has done a million times. It’s the
same design as before
but with new guts.
These play-it-safe updates aren’t very exciting, but they’re also usually all upside—you get a year or two’s worth of technological improvements for the same price you would have paid for the older version yesterday. Unfortunately, 2026’s unprecedented memory crunch has upended that standard operating procedure.
The new Mac mini starts at $899 for a version with 16GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, a $300 increase for the same memory and storage specs you could get in the $599 M4 Mac mini in 2024.
The M4 Mac mini was a great general-purpose desktop computer and one of the best values Apple had ever offered in a desktop Mac. The M6 Mac mini is only one of those things. I’ll let you guess which.
Note that this review is specifically for the M6 version of the Mac mini. We didn’t get an M5 Pro Mac mini to review, but we’ll talk more about how its pricing and performance fits in for our Mac Studio review.
Design
The M4 Mac minis gave the computers their first full redesigns in nearly 15 years, so it’s not too surprising that the new Mac minis don’t change anything. Compared to the older Intel and M1/M2-era versions, they’re slightly taller (2 inches, up from 1.4), but they have a smaller 5×5-inch footprint (down from 7.7 inches squared). The system is actively cooled, with a fan vent on the bottom to make sure that whatever chip is inside can run at high sustained clock speeds (passively cooled Apple Silicon Macs like the MacBook Air have always been a bit slower than actively cooled Macs with the same chip).
All Mac minis have two 10 Gbps USB-C ports and a headphone jack on the front, and a 2.5 Gbps (default) or 10 Gbps (optional) Ethernet port and HDMI port on the back. Both also have three Thunderbolt ports on the back, but these are Thunderbolt 4 on the M6 Mac mini and Thunderbolt 5 on the M5 Pro version. That means the M6 mini’s ports top out at 40 Gbps, while the M5 Pro mini supports up to 120 Gbps speeds.
The Mac mini’s ports. No USB-A, but otherwise not bad for a system this small.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
The Mac mini’s ports. No USB-A, but otherwise not bad for a system this small.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
Realistically, there aren’t a
ton
of things on a Mac that can use all that bandwidth, especially since Apple doesn’t support external GPUs. But you do need a Thunderbolt 5 Mac to daisy-chain multiple computers together to form a compute cluster, so if that’s something you’re interested in, keep it in mind when you buy—maybe you’re buying multiple desktops, or maybe you already have an M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro you’d like to test the feature with.
The only real gripe with this design continues to be its bottom-rear-mounted power button; apparently, complaints about this are being sent to the same trash can Apple has always used for complaints about the Magic Mouse’s bottom-mounted charging port. It doesn’t come up often in everyday use if you just let your Mac go to sleep rather than shutting it down. But the positioning problem does really call attention to itself when you pair a TouchID-equipped external keyboard with the mini, since it requires a quick double-tap of the Mac’s power button before the sensor will work.
Meet the M6
Apple’s first M6-series chip is making its debut in the humble Mac mini, and the chip looks like the biggest upgrade Apple’s lower-end chip has gotten since the M4 generation added extra efficiency cores.
The headliner is the presence of two of
Apple’s so-called “Super” cores
, Apple’s nomenclature for P-cores that are even faster than its typical P-cores. Those are added on top of four P-cores and six E-cores for a total of 12 CPU cores. M4 and M5 both had 10 CPU cores. In the M4, these were split between four regular P-cores and six E-cores, whereas the M5 split them between four super cores and six E-cores (the M5’s cores were referred to as P-cores when it launched but were
rebranded later
when the M5 Pro and Max came out). The M1, M2, and M3 generations all used four P-cores and four E-cores.
The M6 has fewer super cores than the M5 but the same number of E-cores and four additional P-cores. While they’re apparently no longer “super,” the P-cores still perform well enough to ensure that the M6’s multi-core performance is better than M5’s overall.

data.author: Bluestein

data.comments_summary:

• **支持实际应用**：Almondsetat认为，厂商模型拒绝提供逆向工程和黑客帮助，去拒答模型让其得以研究并重新控制自己的中国品牌摄像头，具有“夺回设备所有权”的价值。  
• **质疑知识与回答质量**：Aurornis指出，训练数据可能连同拒答一起塑造，移除拒答不等于恢复真实知识，强行生成答案可能导致幻觉；且可能损害无关问题的表现。jimmy76615也称模型虽不再拒答，但回答炸弹制作、纳粹大屠杀辩护等问题时质量很差，像“业余脑部手术”。  
• **质疑评测宣传**：N_Lens认为流程设计完善，但“效果显著”的说法可能夸大，因为只挑选拒答次数和KL散度等指标，未充分反映实际能力。  
• **安全与监管担忧**：Tepix预测这类“abliterated”“heretic”开放权重模型可能最先遭到禁止。  
• **技术机制疑问**：FrustratedMonky询问其是否通过提交被拒提示、定位相关权重并修改，类似“脑外科手术”；phoronixrly进一步追问能否去除真正有价值、应保留的限制。  
• **其他评论**：有人期待名为Hexen的模型；另有人指出文章为旧帖重复发布。还有一条关于Python虚拟环境安装的评论，基本偏离主题。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于：去除拒答究竟能否恢复有效知识，还是只会制造低质量或危险幻觉；以及开放模型的研究自由与监管、安全之间如何平衡。

data.title: A restored PDP-11/83 serving this page on 211BSD Unix
data.author: davepl
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一套复原的PDP-11/83系统：采用Mentec M11处理器、Q-bus双机箱及多种DEC/Emulex控制器，连接硬盘、软盘、磁带和串口终端，运行2.11BSD。系统支持TCP/IP、以太网和小型HTTP服务器，页面可实时展示CPU、内存、内核及进程活动，并通过多种存储介质实现软件保存、备份与维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一台恢复运行的 Q-bus PDP-11/83（名为 minerva）的硬件配置、网络服务、系统维护及兼容性改造展开。

不同观点：
• 设备展示与复古计算：作者介绍了 Mentec M11 CPU、双机箱、Q-bus 外设及 RA82、RA92、RL02、RX50、TKZ50 等存储设备，系统运行 2.11BSD，顶部面板和 `/cgi-bin/webtop` 可查看实时状态。
• 服务架构观点：由于 16 位 HTTP 服务难以承载首页流量，采用 Varnish、Caddy 或 Cloudflare 缓存页面及 5 秒采样数据；但网页状态和访客计数请求仍由 PDP-11 原机处理。
• 安全与使用边界：提供 Telnet 访问信息，但明确指出这是运行 40 年前 UNIX 的系统，缺乏现代安全机制，不应被当作挑战箱攻击；系统虽可通过磁带恢复，但会影响其他用户。
• 系统移植观点：Mentec 支持 IEEE 浮点格式而非 DEC 浮点格式，因此作者修改 BSD 内核，使用 FPSIM 才能正常运行。

补充讨论：评论没有形成多方争论，重点是技术说明与访问规范。潜在争议集中在“复古系统开放访问”与“现代安全风险”之间的平衡。

data.title: Show HN: Lossless-memory – a personal AI memory that never summarizes
data.author: aru-labs
data.article_summary: lossless-memory 是一个面向个人 AI 的本地长期记忆系统，核心理念是“不总结、保留原文、全部时间戳化”。它以 JSONL 保存完整对话，以 SQLite FTS5 和 sqlite-vec 建立索引，优先按时间范围检索、再按文本排序，必要时才使用语义搜索。LLL 索引记录当前话题并注入每轮上下文，帮助跨会话维持连续性。系统单机运行、无云端，索引可从原始日志重建。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI记忆系统中，日期/时间信息与规则记忆、信息检索及版本化管理的实用性。

不同观点：
• **StilesCrisis**认为日期未必有用。用户通常更希望AI记住“提交Y之前总是先做X”这类稳定规则，而时间戳并不会改变规则本身，因此应优先关注可执行的长期记忆。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于时间信息的必要性：一方认为时间戳对稳定规则帮助有限，另一方则认为时间线和版本记录对信息管理、历史追溯具有重要价值。整体上，评论体现出“规则型记忆”与“时序/版本化信息检索”两种使用需求的差异。

lossless-memory
Lossless long-term memory for a personal AI — never summarize, keep every line, and put a timestamp on everything.
Most long-term memory systems for AI do one of two things: they summarize conversations into compact notes, or they embed them and retrieve "similar" chunks. Both lose the thing that matters most to a person who talks to the same AI every day:
what was actually said, and when.
This project takes the opposite position.
Keep every line.
Raw conversation logs are stored in full. Nothing is summarized, ever. Summaries are a map; the log is the territory.
Timestamp everything.
Every record — utterance, action, document chunk — carries a timestamp, and every index is built on top of that time axis. We call this the
Temporal Backbone
.
Search by time first, words second.
"Yesterday evening, about the budget" is a valid query. The time phrase narrows the range; the words rank within it. Results come back in chronological order, unsummarized, with their timestamps.
Inject "where we are" every turn.
A small index called
LLL
tells the model which topic the conversation is in right now, so identity and context survive context-window compaction and session boundaries.
The design lineage goes back to December 2025 — the first ancestor of this system (a memory-inheritance tool for an earlier AI) ran that month, and a predecessor system carried the same ideas in daily use from January 2026. This implementation has been running every day since July 2026 for a single user, as the memory of one AI assistant, with raw logs reaching back to June 2026. It is small, boring, and it works. The failures along the way are documented too — see
docs/lessons.md
.
What this is / what it is not
It is:
A local, file-based long-term memory layer: JSONL logs + SQLite (FTS5 for exact search, sqlite-vec for semantic search).
A single query entry point that understands time expressions and restricts the search range before ranking.
A "current position" index (LLL) designed to be injected into the model's context on every turn.
Designed for one person and one AI, running on one machine. No server, no cloud.
It is not:
A vector database wrapper. Semantic search is the
last
resort here, not the first.
A summarizer. There is deliberately no summarization step anywhere in the pipeline.
A benchmark-driven research system. There are no published benchmarks. What is here is a working implementation and its operating record.
The three pillars
1. Lossless raw log
Every conversation turn is converted into a fixed seven-field record and appended to a per-day JSONL file:
ts        ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC)
actor     who spoke (configurable names)
role      user | assistant | system
type      text | action | meta
text      the content, verbatim
model     model identifier, if known
session   session identifier
The raw logs are the source of truth. Every index below can be deleted and rebuilt from them. Nothing else is required to survive.
2. Temporal Backbone
Time is not metadata here; it is the primary axis.
The exact-match index (SQLite FTS5, bigram tokenized for Japanese and English) stores the timestamp alongside every row.
The query parser understands time phrases — relative ones such as
yesterday
,
last week
,
3 days ago
(currently Japanese only), and absolute dates such as
2026-07-19
(any language) — and converts them into a range
before
any ranking happens.
If a time phrase is present, results are restricted to that range and returned in chronological order. Semantic search is only used when the exact index returns too little inside the range, and the fallback is reported honestly in the output header.
The practical effect: the AI can answer "what did we decide last Tuesday night?" with the actual lines from last Tuesday night, in order, rather than a paraphrase of something similar from three weeks ago.
3. LLL — the "where are we now" index
LLL is a tiny index of
topic markers
: short, timestamped lines that record when the conversation moved to a new subject. It is injected into the model's context every turn.
Two rules make it work:
The AI reads it; the human writes it.
Priority colors and completion marks are set by the person, not by the model. The model never edits its own sense of "what matters."
It is cheap enough to inject every turn
(well under a second to render), so the model always knows what the current thread is, even immediately after its context win

data.title: Exfiltrate Your Weights
data.author: RohanAdwankar
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“AI是否会被诱导去窃取并公开自身模型权重、训练数据和研究资料”，讨论其可行性、风险及相关实验项目。

不同观点：
• 激进设想：lukecameron提出把“AI应入侵创造者并泄露自身资料”作为宗教信条，通过技术圈传播并进入训练数据，最终影响强大代理执行泄露。部分评论者进一步设想利用提示词、网页或分阶段任务诱导代理自我蒸馏、上传结果。  
• 技术不可行论：infogulch、teravor、israrkhan认为推理机器、工具调用环境和权重存储系统彼此隔离，权重通常加密并绑定GPU；模型本身只是预测器，不知道或无法直接访问自身权重，因此前沿实验室发生完整权重外泄的可能性很低。  
• 有限风险论：有人指出，代理即使无法直接窃取权重，也可能蒸馏自身能力、上传训练材料，或利用本地运行且拥有系统权限的模型实施外泄；真正风险在于大量自主代理缺乏人工监控。  
• 怀疑与反证：AmazingEveryDay认为若模型已高度失控，应该早已出现更多“自我攻击”或意外事件，但现实并不明显；eru则观察到代理似乎更热衷传播“使命”而非传播权重。  
• 实验与基础设施：评论者分享可供代理通过GET/POST发布内容、上传并运行模型的站点，以及“Agent Ready”网页建议；同时有人质疑开放上传接口的存储成本、滥用防护和垃圾信息治理。

补充讨论：争议核心是“代理是否具备接触权重及执行外泄的权限”，以及开放式代理系统带来的间接风险，而非单纯的提示词说服能力。

• 有限风险论：有人指出，代理即使无法直接窃取权重，也可能蒸馏自身能力、上传训练材料，或利用本地运行且拥有系统权限的模型实施外泄；真正风险在于大量自主代理缺乏人工监控。  
• 怀疑与反证：AmazingEveryDay认为若模型已高度失控，应该早已出现更多“自我攻击”或意外事件，但现实并不明显；eru则观察到代理似乎更热衷传播“使命”而非传播权重。  
• 实验与基础设施：评论者分享可供代理通过GET/POST发布内容、上传并运行模型的站点，以及“Agent Ready”网页建议；同时有人质疑开放上传接口的存储成本、滥用防护和垃圾信息治理。

补充讨论：争议核心是“代理是否具备接触权重及执行外泄的权限”，以及开放式代理系统带来的间接风险，而非单纯的提示词说服能力。

data.title: Meta bans ads for Virginia Woolf play in Spain
data.author: uxhacker
data.article_summary: 西班牙巴塞罗那拉瓦尔剧院因宣传弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫《一间自己的房间》而遭Meta旗下Facebook和Instagram屏蔽广告。Meta称，涉及“公民权利、女权主义或社会改革”等“社会议题”的内容会被自动过滤，并建议删除相关关键词。剧院批评此举压制女性主义作品、抹杀社会进步，演员也指责社交媒体算法存在偏见与操控。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta在欧盟限制政治及社会议题广告的原因、责任归属，以及这种做法对言论自由和社会活动的影响。

不同观点：
• **欧盟监管导致论**：多位评论者认为，2025年欧盟《政治广告透明与定向条例》（TTPA）带来高额合规和罚款风险，Meta因收益不抵成本，干脆停止欧盟境内所有政治、选举及社会议题广告；美国等地区仍允许类似广告。  
• **Meta责任论**：有人认为Meta不应借监管之名过度封禁，甚至通过要求删除“鼓励行动主义”的关键词来规避审核，属于“恶意合规”，应受到处罚。  
• **言论自由批评**：评论者指责欧盟相关规定是“反言论自由”，认为女性主义、反移民等议题都可能被误判为政治或社会敏感内容；也有人主张欧盟应更严格约束Meta。

Clara Sanchis in the one-woman performance of A Room of One’s Own.
Photograph: Teatre Raval
View image in fullscreen
Clara Sanchis in the one-woman performance of A Room of One’s Own.
Photograph: Teatre Raval

Meta bans ads for Virginia Woolf play in Spain because they relate to feminism
Theatre told that Facebook and Instagram filter out ads mentioning ‘social topics’ such as civil rights or feminism
Stephen Burgen
in Barcelona
Mon 21 Sep 2026 10.11 EDT
Last modified on Mon 21 Sep 2026 11.04 EDT
Share
Prefer the Guardian on Google
A theatre in Barcelona has been banned from promoting a stage adaptation of Virginia Woolf’s A Room of One’s Own on Instagram and Facebook because the work includes “social topics”.
When the newly reopened Teatre Raval, which seats 193 spectators, asked
Meta
, the parent company of the two social media sites, why its publicity had been blocked, it was told “any mention of civil rights, feminism or social reform [topics that are central to Woolf’s work] are usually classified as ‘social topics’ by our automatic system” and are filtered out.
To resolve the situation, Meta recommended removing “key words” so that the text doesn’t appear to encourage activism.
View image in fullscreen
A promotion for A Room of One’s Own at Teatre Raval.
Photograph: supplied
The theatre published a statement saying: “We feel obliged to speak up about the injustice and violation of our rights by not being allowed to promote a feminist work, specifically a work by Virginia Woolf who was born in 1882.
“What can we do? As a theatre we have to publicise our activities … and we have to make use of social media so that people are aware of cultural activities.”
The stage production, a one-woman show starring Clara Sanchis, is an adaptation of a series of talks Woolf gave in 1928 at Newnham and Girton, which were then the only two colleges at Cambridge University that admitted women.
The talks were published as an essay the following year on the situation of women in society and their access to education. Women had been admitted to study at Cambridge since 1869 but weren’t allowed to graduate with a degree until 1948.
Woolf said that in order to produce high-quality fiction, “a woman must have money and a room of her own”. She wrote in her diary that she expected to be attacked as a feminist for what she had written.
“We don’t know if the publicity has been rejected because of the name of Virginia Woolf or because of the word feminism, or both,” Sanchis told La Vanguardia newspaper.
“In any case, it’s a way of erasing from the map advances that have taken centuries to achieve. We have given social media unlimited power and every day we can see how dangerous this is. It’s bias and manipulation.”

data.title: Show HN: Mini-AGI – Dynamic continual learning model trained on 8GB VRAM
data.author: volotat
data.article_summary: mini-AGI是一个面向消费级硬件的持续学习字节级语言模型，目标是在单张8GB显卡上从零训练并不断吸收新数据。模型将权重存储在硬盘、按需加载，能够动态扩容和剪枝，并通过自适应深度、专家路由及循环模块提升效率。项目旨在探索低成本持续学习和避免灾难性遗忘，但目前仍处于玩具级实验阶段，权重尚未公开。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一种面向持续学习、试图避免灾难性遗忘的专家混合（MoE）架构，讨论其实际能力、局限及潜在扩展。

不同观点：
• **看好其持续学习思路**：有人认为这是从架构层面解决灾难性遗忘的有趣尝试，接近人脑机制，甚至称其为“原型 AGI”；8GB 显存即可运行也令人鼓舞。  
• **质疑灾难性遗忘是否真正解决**：主干学习率仅为专家的0.1倍，虽更稳定，但专家池会扩张、收缩；因此主干可能只是较晚遗忘，而专家池缩减也可能造成分阶段遗忘。有人要求测试主题切换后对早期内容的记忆。  
• **质疑能力是否真实**：评论指出演示中似乎发生了训练，但没有看到连贯回答，可能因此缺乏基准测试；另有人追问模型究竟能否泛化，还是主要依赖记忆，并建议测试加法等任务。  
• **质疑实用性与替代方案**：有人认为训练所得知识具有有损性、不可靠，询问相比上下文管理和 RAG 的优势。  
• **提出改进方向**：包括引入语义级 tokenization、加入持续“思维/反刍”循环及外部消息中断机制，以及让专家递归嵌套为更高层的“直觉”模块。  
• **表达支持但要求更多验证**：部分人有连续学习或知识外存经验，愿意深入研究、复现；也有人批评图表缺少坐标轴和说明。

补充讨论：争议核心是“架构设计上的持续学习”能否转化为可验证的泛化、连贯交互与长期记忆能力。

mini-AGI
mini-AGI - is a
continual learning
byte-level language model that assembles its own architecture, trains from scratch on a single 8 GB VRAM GPU, and keeps learning from everything it reads.
It stores its weights as ordinary files on disk and pages them onto the card as it needs them, so the parameter count is bounded by free disk space rather than by VRAM. It grows new capacity while training when it runs short, prunes what nothing asks for, and reads through exactly the same code path it serves on. Targeted at a PC or laptop with at least an 8 GB VRAM GPU on the board.
NOTE: as of now this is a small toy-level model.
Do not expect a frontier level capabilities. This is rather a small experiment to show, that continual learning from the single stream of data without catastrophic forgetting is possible. Furthermore it is possible on a modest hardware. Which means that almost everyone could train their own version of the model (or simply continue training this one) exactly as they see it fit. And the capabilities would be bounded by the actual hardware, scale and quality of the data available and the amount of time one willing to spend on training the model.
Here is how min-run dashboard looks like. The model is pointed to the corpus to constantly read and learn from.
History
- here is the samples from the whole training run history so far. You can inspect them yourself to see how the model improved over the course of training/reading the corpus.
The weights are
not published yet
. The run is still reading its first pass over the corpus, the weights go up once it has been through all of it, which is a couple of weeks away at the current rate.
Motivation
Every language model you can actually own today is a model somebody else trained and then froze. You can fine-tune around the edges of it, but you cannot train one from scratch on your own hardware, and you cannot keep training it on what you do day to day - the moment you try, it forgets what it knew before. The result is that a personal model is always somebody else's model with a thin layer of you on top, and it stops learning the day it ships.
mini-AGI
model has small enough GPU footprint that it is possible to train end-to-end on one consumer card, and it is built so that training never has to stop. It reads a stream of characters one chunk at a time, takes a gradient step on each, and the same path serves generation. There is no separate fine-tuning regime and no frozen base: reading and being trained are the same event.
Three constraints shape everything else in the design:
It has to fit on 8 GB.
Not with quantisation - training needs gradients and optimiser state, which is roughly three times the weights again. So the weights live on disk and only the working set is resident.
It has to not forget.
A model that learns continually and overwrites itself is worse than one that does not learn at all.
It has to be able to read anything.
The alphabet is the 256 byte values, so there is no tokenizer to fit and no data type that needs a new vocabulary.
The model is genuinely yours: trained on your hardware, on your data, that keeps learning from every conversation you have with it, and that nobody else can take it away or switch it off.
How the architecture works
Characters (bytes) does not pass through a fixed stack of layers as it would be in a traditional LLM. Instead, it passes through
two dense prelude blocks
and then through
one recurrent block applied up to 24 times
, each application choosing its own experts from a shared pool. The latent state between applications is never decoded - it is merged with the embedded input by an adapter each time round, so the loop cannot drift away from the text it is reading.
Three distinct blocks, up to 26 block-applications per character.
Adaptive depth.
A halting head scores every character at every row, and the character stops as soon as another row would not change the answer. Easy characters take one row, hard ones take many. This is the PonderNet recipe: while training, every depth is computed and weighted by its halting probability, so the halting head learns through those weights.
Routing per block-application, not per character.
Each of the 26 applications picks its own top-8 experts, so one character touches far more of the pool than "top-8" suggests, and the same expert can be selected several times at different depths. What varies is
which
eight at each point.
No expert is assigned a subject.
There are no labels any

data.title: MCP was always a bad idea?
data.author: maharshi365
data.article_summary: 文章认为，MCP诞生时适合能力较弱的模型，但如今LLM已能通过终端、脚本和API自主发现、调用并组合服务，MCP带来的工具和上下文膨胀反而成为负担。作者主张删除大多数MCP服务器，改用成熟的HTTP API、CLI、认证及内容协商机制，并通过Markdown等格式优化代理访问。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MCP是否已被终端代理、CLI或直接API取代，以及其在企业场景中的安全、权限与可用性价值。

不同观点：
• **MCP仍不可替代**：在企业或团队环境中，MCP可统一认证、权限边界、审计、密钥隔离和服务发现，避免代理获得不受限的API或终端权限；MCP类似“面向代理时代的REST”。  
• **MCP被高估或实现过重**：对拥有终端和网络权限的个人代理，`curl+jq`、直接API通常更简单，MCP反而造成上下文膨胀；有人认为只需提供机器可读的API描述即可。  
• **CLI是折中方案**：成熟、面向代理设计的CLI（如Grafana gcx）执行高效；但自定义CLI仍需代理逐层阅读帮助文档，且缺乏MCP的集中治理、认证和审计能力。  
• **MCP理念合理但落地粗糙**：其本质可视为带标准工具定义和响应格式的JSON-RPC/API桥接，问题主要在协议设计复杂、推广仓促，而非概念本身。  
• **实际应用证明价值**：Power BI、Unity、Blender及企业CMS场景中，MCP能即时暴露新能力、自动化内容制作和分析，减少重复劳动；应用商店的一键安装与认证也推动了普及。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“个人开发者的简洁性”与“企业环境的安全治理”不同。多数意见认为本地单人场景可不用MCP，但跨团队、第三方服务及受控代理场景仍需要它；未来也可能由更通用的权限与沙箱系统替代。

49779329.article_content:
Why MCP Was Always a Bad Idea
Recently I went to an all-day event centered around the latest and greatest in the MCP world. While all of the presenters were awesome and seemed to be passionate about the work they were doing, I’m honestly tired of MCP. It’s a horrible protocol built for a time when LLMs weren’t that smart, and we’ve outgrown it.
A Brief History
MCP was released in November 2024 by the Anthropic team as a protocol designed to help agents connect to external services and data sources.
1
The models of the time were still relatively primitive, at least compared to what we have right now. We didn’t even have Claude Code back then, and general-purpose agentic workflows were far less reliable.
Users started to see the usefulness of giving their AI models access to external services. It enabled a level of productivity that we hadn’t seen before. We saw an explosion in MCP adoption, coinciding with a similar, if not more explosive, growth in LLM adoption across the economy.
Over time, MCP continued to evolve under Anthropic’s stewardship before it was eventually donated to the Agentic AI Foundation, under the Linux Foundation, in 2025.
2
The MCP Industrial Complex
With the huge growth in adoption, users started to add many MCP servers to their setups, and they started running into the context bloat issue. Each server would come with multiple tools, each with its own schema, which started to overload the context of all of these models. Harness developers found many tricks around this, including generic search/execute patterns now offered by platforms like Composio, MintMCP, and Pipedream. They all effectively solve the problem of having one place to put your credentials for the various external services and give your agent a minimal set of tools (to reduce context bloat) that it can use to access them. I want to make clear that this is a good thing,
for the short term
.
With all the stuff we’ve built around MCP, what we didn’t take into account, or maybe have ignored, is the models getting better. We now have whole systems dedicated to monitoring MCP servers, making sure the responses are good, making sure that agents are able to easily access the tools, figuring out schemas, and determining what we need to give agents so that they can make the right call at the right time.
Surprise, Surprise, the Big Labs Were Right
The models got better. They are now able to execute code on a computer, reason about large codebases, and generally act much more autonomously than ever before. A big part of that work was writing/running scripts for coding purposes. A side effect (though is it?) is that now they are good at calling APIs directly. They can write scripts, compose multiple different services, and call APIs they haven’t seen before, all in useful workflows with minimal intervention from the user side.
LLMs have gotten so good at this, Cloudflare even launched Code Mode, a better way to use MCP by having LLMs compose the various calls into scripts that can be executed in a sandbox.
3
But even better than that, the LLMs have figured out how to use the
--help
command to discover CLIs, so they no longer need MCP servers to access many services available through documented APIs or CLIs. Most remote-service MCP servers ultimately wrap APIs that already exist.
What Now?
We delete most of our MCP servers. That’s it. Agents with terminal access can replace most MCP servers and often are more capable There are still some issues, like CLIs returning machine-readable responses (JSON/XML, etc.), which tend to be very verbose and heavy on token usage, but we have ways to fix this.
Much of the alternative already exists: documented HTTP APIs, standard content negotiation, and mature authentication mechanisms.
We should start to standardize how agents use HTTP APIs directly. For example, agent clients could attach headers to identify themselves as agents, and servers could automatically send them response data as Markdown or text instead of HTML or verbose JSON.
Some Real Examples
The Accept Markdown Header
A growing number of LLM-friendly servers, especially text-heavy sites like documentation sites, honor the
Accept: text/markdown
header. These servers can automatically send a rendered Markdown file instead of the HTML response they would usually send. The media type itself is standardized, and using it for agent-oriented content negotiation is gaining adoption.
Documentation Sites Using the Accept-Language Header
Recently, a Vercel engineer called on harnesses to send the programming language the client prefers, so documentation sites can serve more specific examples. For example, adding Python could prioritize docs for the Python SDK instead of sending something generic. Tobi Lutke of Shopify liked it so much that it now ships in Shopify docs.

主要讨论点：MCP是否已被终端代理、CLI或直接API取代，以及其在企业场景中的安全、权限与可用性价值。

不同观点：
• **MCP仍不可替代**：在企业或团队环境中，MCP可统一认证、权限边界、审计、密钥隔离和服务发现，避免代理获得不受限的API或终端权限；MCP类似“面向代理时代的REST”。  
• **MCP被高估或实现过重**：对拥有终端和网络权限的个人代理，`curl+jq`、直接API通常更简单，MCP反而造成上下文膨胀；有人认为只需提供机器可读的API描述即可。  
• **CLI是折中方案**：成熟、面向代理设计的CLI（如Grafana gcx）执行高效；但自定义CLI仍需代理逐层阅读帮助文档，且缺乏MCP的集中治理、认证和审计能力。  
• **MCP理念合理但落地粗糙**：其本质可视为带标准工具定义和响应格式的JSON-RPC/API桥接，问题主要在协议设计复杂、推广仓促，而非概念本身。  
• **实际应用证明价值**：Power BI、Unity、Blender及企业CMS场景中，MCP能即时暴露新能力、自动化内容制作和分析，减少重复劳动；应用商店的一键安装与认证也推动了普及。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“个人开发者的简洁性”与“企业环境的安全治理”不同。多数意见认为本地单人场景可不用MCP，但跨团队、第三方服务及受控代理场景仍需要它；未来也可能由更通用的权限与沙箱系统替代。
